svg.aria-label: A world map with one Postgres primary per region, placed on their real coordinates: Americas in New York, Europe in Paris, and India (APAC) in Mumbai. A dashed circle around Western Europe marks a zoomed inset, since Paris and Amsterdam sit too close together at world scale: the inset shows the global warehouse, co-located in Amsterdam, as a separate node from the Paris primary. Each region's primary key includes the region, so no two regions ever mint the same row. Each primary streams read-only, asynchronously, into the Amsterdam warehouse for reporting, the same consolidation pattern as part 2 of this series, not a write path.
svg.text: One writer per region: conflicts avoided by construction
asynchronous, read-only — never a write path back
No row is ever owned by two regions: the primary key includes the region.
Nothing here resolves a conflict, because nothing here can produce one.
